title: Unexpected headroom collapse — emergency response, RCA and mitigation roadmap
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-09 21:12 UTC we observed a rapid drop in available headroom across three Dedicated pools (EU-west-1 and us-west-2) that triggered sustained request throttling and increased tail latency for large customers on reserved capacity. The platform reported healthy node counts, but the autoscaler stopped provisioning new capacity due to a negative headroom calculation returned by the headroom service. Impact: several high-throughput tenants experienced 20–60% request rejections and 3–7x latency increases for large-sequence requests during the 30-minute window.

Detection & timeline:
- 2026-03-09 21:10 UTC: Synthetic canary latency alarm (per-pool) started to trend upward; on-call received first alert.
- 2026-03-09 21:12 UTC: Customer SLO alerts for reserved-tier customers fired.
- 2026-03-09 21:15 UTC: Observability dashboards showed node counts steady but queue length and token wait time spiking.
- 2026-03-09 21:18 UTC: Incident triage declared; manual mitigation started.
- 2026-03-09 21:25 UTC: Emergency policy applied to temporarily increase max pool size and disable aggressive downscale.
- 2026-03-09 21:40–21:55 UTC: Traffic recovered as extra nodes entered and KV cache warmed.
- 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC: Full incident review snapshot captured and telemetry archived for RCA.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- Temporarily set autoscaler.downscale_window_seconds = 600 (from 120) to prevent oscillatory downsizing.
- Disabled the new short-smoothing-window telemetry path introduced in runtime agent v3.2.1.
- Expanded emergency reservoir (pre-warmed GPU VMs) allocation for EU-west-1 by +4 nodes.
- Manual routing to alternate model variant with lower memory footprint for a subset of reserved customers.

Root cause (summary):
A configuration change landed in runtime agent v3.2.1 that switched the per-request telemetry aggregator from a 30s exponentially-weighted average (alpha tuned for steady state) to a 5s aggressive smoothing window intended to improve latency visibility for short spikes. The autoscaler relies on a headroom service that consumes that telemetry and applies a floor/quantize function when aggregating recent utilization. Under bursty traffic with heterogeneous sequence lengths the new smoothing window produced short-lived negative headroom artifacts (due to rounding/quantization + stale reserve accounting for reserved customers). The autoscaler interpreted negative headroom as a signal that no new nodes were required and suppressed scale-ups while nodes still had warmup/initialization lag. In short: a telemetry smoothing regression combined with the headroom quantization semantics produced an incorrect 'no headroom' decision.

Contributing factors:
- Lack of integration test covering smoothing-window changes against autoscaler headroom semantics.
- Downscale aggressiveness assumed stable metrics; short smoothing increased false-negative headroom signals.
- No per-pool circuit breaker to force emergency reservoir usage when queue length exceeded threshold despite computed headroom.
- Recent change to reserved-customer accounting (to preserve capacity) introduced a timing window where reserve tokens were temporarily double-counted as unavailable during telemetry handoff.

Post-incident action items (owners & timeline):
1) Revert or hotfix telemetry smoothing change in runtime agent v3.2.1 to restore 30s EWMA default and add a feature flag for 5s smoothing. Owner: @diego (patch ready). Due: 2026-03-16.
2) Fix headroom service quantize/floor logic to saturate at a safe minimum (>= 1 node equivalent) and add unit tests for negative/edge cases. Owner: @mina (Headroom team). Due: 2026-03-20.
3) Add a per-pool emergency circuit-breaker: if queue_length_tokens > 2M OR avg_token_wait_ms > 800 for 60s then bypass normal headroom calculation and trigger reservoir allocation. Owner: @kai. Due: 2026-03-24.
4) Implement canary integration test that deploys runtime agent changes against a staging autoscaler with synthetic burst load and validates headroom monotonicity and non-negative invariants. Owner: @testing-squad. Due: 2026-04-01.
5) Alerting & dashboards: new alert for 'headroom_negative_events' with severity P0 and 1-minute aggregation; dashboard tile showing headroom delta vs nodes. Owner: @ops. Due: 2026-03-18.
6) Capacity reservation hardening: ensure reserved-customer accounting handoff includes an acknowledgement handshake to avoid transient double-counting. Owner: @platform-accounts. Due: 2026-03-21.
7) Run an ops tabletop exercise for dedicated-pool headroom failure modes (include PMs and SREs). Owner: @sre-lead. Due: 2026-03-30.

Planned long-term mitigations (quarter roadmap):
- <Q2> Introduce an 'autoscale canary' rollout system: autoscaler config changes must be A/B tested in staging with synthetic and real traffic subsets.
- <Q2> Implement model-aware headroom: headroom service will incorporate model memory footprint and KV-cache warmup windows when calculating effective capacity.
- <Q3> Reservoir expansion and automated pre-warming jitter strategy to reduce node warmup tail latency.
- <Q3> Formal contract tests between runtime telemetry semantics and autoscaler expectations (a small test harness in CI).

Follow-up notes and decisions captured during review meeting (2026-03-14):
- We will not roll back runtime agent v3.2.1 fully; instead we will toggle the smoothing-window flag and ship the headroom saturation fix. Rationale: v3.2.1 includes valuable observability improvements we want to keep.
- Agreed SLA communication: customer success will notify impacted reserved customers with a summary and action plan by 2026-03-16.
- Add compliance note: no secrets or customer data were exposed during this incident.

Attached artifacts and references (links below) provide raw telemetry, synthetic canary graphs, and the emergency PR that was applied during the incident.

notes: Preserve telemetry snapshots for 90 days for forensic replay.
We should add an invariant check in CI: headroom >= -0.5 * node_capacity_equivalent should never be allowed; prefer non-negative enforcement.
Consider adding per-tenant soft-fallback model routing when dedicated headroom drops below 10% for 120s.
